name: RaptorDB
tagline: Embedded .NET JSON document store with compiled C# views and automatic bitmap indexes; inactive since 2019.
description: RaptorDB is Mehdi Gholam's open-source document database for .NET, introduced through a long-running CodeProject article in 2012. Applications store plain C# objects as JSON documents and define views as compiled .NET map functions; RaptorDB maintains those views with automatic hybrid bitmap indexes and lets you filter them with LINQ predicates, so queries feel native to C# code. Later versions added a standalone server mode, transactions, backup and active restore, server-side queries, Mono/Android support and headquarters-to-branch replication. The last tagged version, 4.0.10, landed in October 2019 and the project has been dormant since, so it is best treated as a reference design rather than a dependency.
statusNote: No commits since October 2019 (v4.0.10). For embedded .NET storage consider LiteDB, RavenDB or SQLite.

scale.notes: Single process or server; replication is HQ-to-branch copying rather than clustering.

strengths: Views are compiled C# map functions, so indexing logic is type-checked code
Automatic bitmap indexes on view columns make LINQ filters fast
Runs embedded or as a server with the same API
Built-in backup, restore and HQ-to-branch replication
weaknesses: Single maintainer and no activity since 2019
Targets older .NET Framework and Mono runtimes
No SQL and only a .NET client
useCases: Maintaining older .NET apps that embed RaptorDB
